Meanwhile EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents explicitly handles destinations without a credentialId by filtering credentials by integration and calling createEvent with that credential's id — such a destination can never match by credentialId, so its externalId is ignored and the event lands on the credential's primary calendar, whereas the old code used `destinationCalendar.externalId` directly. judged_text: createEvent resolves the target calendar solely by matching destinationCalendar entries' credentialId against the passed credentialId and otherwise falls back to 'primary', so a destination calendar with a null credentialId — the case EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents explicitly supports through its integration-filter branch — never matches. Bookings whose destination calendar has no credentialId get their Google event created on the credential's primary calendar instead of the selected destination calendar, while CalendarManager still echoes destination.externalId into the booking reference, so later updates and deletes target a calendar the event was never created in and 404.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, the target calendar is selected only via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and otherwise falls back to `"primary"`. But `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` explicitly supports destinationCalendar entries without `credentialId` (the `else` branch that filters credentials by `destination.integration`), and in that path it calls `createEvent(c, event)` without any externalId hint. As a result, when a destination calendar entry has no `credentialId`, Google event creation cannot select that destination’s `externalId` and will default to the credential’s primary calendar instead of the chosen destination calendar.
